viewport.context: Fresh Playwright context; local file URL; no personal profile or cookies.

actions.action: Clicked “Explore a Web” from the home hero.
actions.observed: The URL moved to #explorer and the page scrolled to the Web Explorer. It presents five proposed cases and an illustrative role set.
actions.taskOutcome: Helped locate the conceptual DEX workflow; it did not open or connect a DEX application.
actions.evidence: Browser action log; supplied explorer.png; visible labels “ILLUSTRATIVE WEB” and “Not proof verification, not acceptance, not settlement.”

actions.action: Selected the “02 / PROPOSED — Batched DEX orders” case.
actions.observed: The selected case text became “Batched DEX orders”; the description asks to connect each order’s exact assets and minimum net receipt to a specified pool transition. The inspector showed “Order arithmetic” with two orders offering 100 A, requiring at least 90 B net, and illustrative 92 B outcomes.
actions.taskOutcome: Helped me understand the intended DEX use case and what a proof role might describe. No concrete proof instance, independent producer, required-set consumer, or integration path appeared.
actions.evidence: My captured and inspected dex-case.png; on-page case paragraph and “INSPECT AN ILLUSTRATED ROLE” panel.

actions.action: Tried clicking the diagram label “Fee accounting.”
actions.observed: The diagram remained on the default Staged invoice escrow case, and the inspector still showed “Payment arithmetic”; clicking the visible Fee accounting label did not change the inspected role.
actions.taskOutcome: Did not help me inspect the Fee accounting explanation. I did not infer that the diagram node was a supported control.
actions.evidence: My captured and inspected fee-accounting-role.png; the inspector heading remains “Payment arithmetic.”

actions.action: Checked then unchecked “Omit this illustrated proof.”
actions.observed: The checkbox changed to checked and then unchecked. The control’s visible helper text calls it “An explanation control, not a transaction action.”
actions.taskOutcome: Clarified that omission only changes the illustration. It did not simulate transaction rejection or demonstrate proof validation.
actions.evidence: Browser interaction log and accessible label “Omit this illustrated proof”; supplied explorer.png.

actions.action: Clicked “Follow the value” in the page navigation.
actions.observed: The URL moved to #worksheet and the page scrolled to the invoice worksheet. The visible figures separate a 35 CASH seller payment, a 2 CASH fee, and a 2 CASH backing gap; it labels the calculation local arithmetic and the source behavior as not executed.
actions.taskOutcome: Useful context for what the example intends a transaction to account for, but it is not DEX-specific executable behavior.

actions.action: Clicked “Developer journey” and opened “Who would use this handoff?” and “Current source commands & proposed interfaces.”
actions.observed: The handoff says it is not a shipping SDK or wallet integration. It describes a workflow from defining an action through evidence mapping to effect readback. The disclosure says the source README documents mori-k2 compile, inspect, setup, prove, and verify, but this page did not execute them; future mori obligations inspect, mori web assemble, and transaction build/submit/observe are proposals, not runnable commands here.
actions.taskOutcome: This answered where the page’s stated implementation boundary lies, while leaving me without a usable DEX integration interface or example.
actions.evidence: Browser interaction log; #developers section and opened disclosure text. developer-journey.png was captured but not visually inspected.

questions.question: What API, library, or adapter does a Cardano DEX call to construct a Web and connect its Strands to the consuming script?
questions.whereItArose: “Explore a Web” and the Batched DEX orders case in the Web Explorer.
questions.answerLocation: The Explorer explains the intended mapping from claim specification to Strand and consuming script; “Current source commands & proposed interfaces” names future mori web assemble as a proposal.
questions.remainingClarification: There is no runnable Web API, DEX adapter, integration sample, or interface contract on this page. Which interface is actually implemented, and where can a developer use it?

questions.question: Which developer-facing commands exist today, and what do they do in a DEX workflow?
questions.whereItArose: “Current source commands & proposed interfaces” under Developer journey.
questions.answerLocation: It says the source README documents mori-k2 compile, inspect, setup, prove, and verify, and says the page did not execute them. It names mori obligations inspect, mori web assemble, and transaction build/submit/observe as future proposals.
questions.remainingClarification: The page does not link or reproduce the README instructions, nor map those commands to a working DEX example. I cannot tell from this page which parts are usable for this task.

questions.question: Are the three DEX roles three independent proofs that the application must produce?
questions.whereItArose: The DEX case’s illustrative role set.
questions.answerLocation: Explorer caption says roles are requirements, not three independent proof producers or concrete Strands; a native whole-execution proof may cover several arithmetic conditions.
questions.remainingClarification: What concrete producer and consumer interfaces implement this relationship in a supported deployment? The page marks them unestablished.

questions.question: Is this a deployed Cardano integration, and does selecting a role perform proof or transaction work?
questions.whereItArose: Hero description and interactive Web Explorer.
questions.answerLocation: Hero calls it a proposed Cardano concept and says general Web integration and onchain settlement are unestablished; role inspector says the omission control is explanatory, not a transaction action.
questions.remainingClarification: No live integration or runnable transaction path is demonstrated; this page gives no deployment or usage entrypoint.

findings.impact: High for a developer deciding whether to integrate: the concept describes the intended data relationship but leaves the actual entrypoint and integration surface unknown.
findings.observation: The DEX case is explicitly illustrative. The developer disclosure lists existing source README commands but says they were not run by the page, and labels Web assembly and transaction commands as future proposals.
findings.evidence: Explorer case “Batched DEX orders”; Developer journey disclosures “Current source commands & proposed interfaces” and “A useful developer handoff.”
findings.suggestedChange: Add a direct link to the current developer README and a small status-tagged DEX handoff showing the first supported command or API, its input/output artifacts, and the first unsupported boundary. If no supported DEX path exists, label the case as a target workflow before the CTA.

findings.impact: Medium: I can understand the target idea, but cannot turn it into an integration task from this page.
findings.observation: The DEX description says to connect exact assets and minimum net receipt to a specified pool transition, but shows no concrete interface example. The page does give a useful conceptual chain: claim specification, statement, Strand, consuming script.
findings.evidence: Web Explorer intro and selected Batched DEX orders case; Developer journey workflow.
findings.suggestedChange: Show one compact, explicitly illustrative mapping from a DEX order’s input fields to the stated claim/Strand/consumer roles, with each unavailable runtime hook labeled. Keep it clearly separate from a supported SDK recipe.

findings.impact: Low: the main CTA can read like an app entrypoint on first glance.
findings.observation: The hero button says “Explore a Web”; the same hero immediately qualifies the page as an interactive concept illustration and says integration and settlement are unestablished. Later labels and caveats are clear.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile top screenshots; hero text immediately below the CTA; explorer screenshot labels the content illustrative.
findings.suggestedChange: Consider “Explore the Web illustration” or add a short “concept walkthrough” label to the CTA so the interactive surface is identified before click.

teachBack: As I understand the page, a Web is a proposed script-bound collection of required Strands for one transition. A claim specification names an assertion and relation; an individual Strand carries a proof claim, statement, and binding metadata, and the consumer must agree with the statement and context. For a DEX, the proposed example connects each order’s exact assets and minimum net receipt to a pool transition. The page gives a design vocabulary and example roles, plus a stated list of source README commands. It does not establish a runnable Cardano DEX integration, Web assembly API, wallet integration, concrete DEX proof producers, on-chain settlement, or that the pictured roles verify anything. The page’s stated current source commands were not executed in my review.
limits: This was a persona-based review of a frozen local HTML artifact, not a real human usability study.
I used a fresh local Playwright Chromium context and inspected only the named site and supplied screenshots plus the required workflow notes.
I did not inspect implementation source, follow external links, run any source commands, prove, sign, connect a wallet, access a network, or assess cryptographic correctness.

I visually inspected the supplied desktop-top.png, mobile-top.png, explorer.png, and my own dex-case.png and follow-the-value.png captures. I captured developer-journey.png but did not visually inspect it.
Clicking the diagram’s Fee accounting label did not change the inspector in my browser; I did not treat that failed attempt as a successful role selection.
